Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{2}{9}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{9} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot [\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})] \\ -\frac{2}{9} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\ -\frac{2}{9} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
